Overall, Jobber is a great platform, but there are several areas that definitely need improvement, particularly with the mobile app, AI Receptionist, client records, and third-party integrations. As a business owner who relies on Jobber daily, these are practical improvements that would make a significant difference in efficiency.  1. Technician Time Tracking  Business owners should be able to view technicians’ time entries and hours worked on individual jobs directly from the mobile app. This information should be readily accessible without having to switch to the desktop version.  2. AI Receptionist Call History  Every incoming call should have a clearly displayed date and timestamp. Phone numbers should also be clickable, allowing us to return calls directly from the AI Receptionist’s call history.  Currently, unless a caller submits an actual request that becomes associated with a client profile, we have to manually copy and paste the phone number to return the call. This is an unnecessary inconvenience that should be easy to correct.  3. Better Integration Between Pages  There needs to be more seamless navigation between AI Receptionist conversations, call history, client profiles, requests, and jobs. Information should be interconnected without requiring users to constantly switch between screens or manually transfer details.  4. Native Mobile Text Messaging  There should be an option to open a customer’s phone number in the device’s native text messaging app rather than being limited to messaging within Jobber.  Many customers initially contact us through regular text messages. Having the flexibility to communicate through our phone’s messaging app, while ideally maintaining a connection to their Jobber client profile, would be extremely valuable.  5. Centralized Client Attachments and Photos  All attachments, including photos and documents uploaded to individual jobs, should automatically populate in a centralized attachment section within the client’s main profile.  Currently, having to open individual jobs to locate previously uploaded photos or documents is unnecessarily time-consuming, especially when a customer has a long service history.  There should be one consolidated list or gallery showing every attachment associated with that customer, regardless of which job it was originally uploaded to. Ideally, each attachment would also link back to its original job for reference.  6. Better Two-Way Integration With CompanyCam  The CompanyCam integration is a great example of a feature that has potential but needs better connectivity.  I appreciate that Jobber can automatically create a corresponding project in CompanyCam. However, there should also be a direct link within the Jobber client or job profile that opens the associated CompanyCam project, and vice versa.  If the integration already connects the two platforms and creates the corresponding project, there should be no reason we can’t navigate directly between them. This would eliminate unnecessary searching and make the integration significantly more useful.  Overall Feedback  These aren’t extravagant feature requests. They’re basic workflow improvements that would save contractors and business owners considerable time throughout the day.  Jobber continues to introduce new features, particularly AI-powered tools, but I believe greater attention needs to be given to improving the functionality, navigation, and integration of the features already available.  A truly efficient platform should make information accessible from wherever you’re working, whether that’s a client’s profile, an individual job, the AI Receptionist, or an integrated application like CompanyCam.  I would really like to see these improvements prioritized and implemented sooner rather than later. Jobber is already a valuable business management tool, but addressing these everyday frustrations would make it substantially better for the contractors who depend on it.

Let’s start with the potential legal problem. I just discovered through way of my most recent estimate that a client can push the estimate to invoice and make a partial payment without signing. This has put me in a spot where I have to ask them to sign after receiving a payment. If they decide they don’t want to sign then I have an agreement issue with my contract because the signature verifies they agree to the terms but I don’t have it. Yet I’ve already received payment so work is still expected. This isn’t even just an annoying thing of get the signature or cancel work and the hassle of refunding which can create bad reviews on my part but also a legal issue. Clients should have to sign the estimate if I have the signature in place to do so before it can go to invoice so that my contract is valid allowing me to protect myself in court should anything happen.   My contract protects by insuring clients are aware of hazards the work creates and removes my liability from injury should they come into the work area, informs them of additional charges for debit and credit charges, bounced checks, let’s the client know that additional charges may be added for any unforeseen damages that could not be detected prior to work and gives me an out if they opt not to pay those additional costs, and many other things to keep me out of court.  I do not like that the client can bypass the signature and feel strongly that this should be corrected. A simple slider (like the “cover credit charges” option) that I can flip that doesn’t allow them to move to invoice until the signature is received.  Other than that I absolutely love this app, I don’t pay for pro but am paying for the mid year. I will be when my current year is up which should be near. My clients have all loved the ease of use it provides and I’ve received numerous jobs because people love how easy it makes working with me. They love that they don’t have to wait for a mailed bill or dropped bill, they can see everything right there and pay right then. They love they way it is itemized giving them a better scope of the work. I honestly feel it would take a severely superior app to pull me away from joist. But for the love of everything please allow me to require signature on estimates prior to invoice or at least don’t allow the client to force it to invoice.
